ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The structure shows a central carbonyl carbon at the junction. An oxygen is drawn above it with a double bond to the central carbon. On the left, the central carbon is bonded to an R substituent. On the right/lower side, the central carbon is bonded to an additional carbon substituent. Curved arrows are present in the drawing, but the question says to ignore the arrows. Reasoning: Replace the left R group with the wildcard atom `*`. Represent the carbonyl as `C=O`, and include the additional carbon substituent as a branch on the carbonyl carbon, `(C)`. Therefore the SMILES expression is `*C(C)=O`.

planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Apply SMILES conventions: R/group attachment in a generic structure can be represented as wildcard `*`; a carbonyl is written as `C=O`; branches from a central atom are placed in parentheses. The connectivity `R-C(=O)-C` can be expressed as `*C(C)=O`.
